title: Mobile Platform for Oral Cancer Screening and Diagnosis in Low and MiddleIncome Countries (LMICs)
text: Oral cancer remains a significant public health challenge in the United States because delayed diagnosis and limited access to effective screening tools can worsen patient outcomes, particularly in U.S. low-resource settings. This project develops a non-invasive, AI-enabled platform for early detection and triage of oral cancer, using high-volume clinical validation in India to generate knowledge, algorithms, and workflows directly applicable to future U.S. dental, primary care, community health, and rural clinical settings. The technology and knowledge generated will improve screening accessibility and clinical outcomes for U.S. populations.

title: Epigenetic Aging: The Impact of Social and Environmental Realism
text:
Animal models are necessary tools for experimental biomedicine, though constant lab environments may be
poor approximations for processes shaping health in complex natural animal or human populations. Recent
work suggests that additional translational relevance can be gained by leveraging the tools of biomedicine on
mouse model populations living in natural outdoor enclosures. Here, we will use this ‘re-wilding’ approach to
establish how the processes of age-related methylation and behavioral senescence differ for mice living in
standard lab versus more natural conditions with the aim of developing more translational aging research.

title: Environmental Toxicology and Epidemiology Pre- and Post-Doctoral Research T32 Training Program
text:
Research & Related Other Project Information
8. Project Narrative
This Environmental Toxicology and Epidemiology Program trains future leaders in the
environmental health sciences (EHS) who accelerate discoveries of how environmental
exposures affect human health and promote improvements in public health. The program
focuses on translational applications to human disease prevention with training that bridges
environmental toxicology (basic research), epidemiology (population-based research), and
exposure sciences.

title: Improving Cancer and Tobacco Cessation Care for Individuals with Serious Mental Illness
text: This research aims to improve treatment for cancer and serious mental illness and identify strategies to increase the reach of person-centered collaborative care and tobacco cessation. This approach has potential to mitigate modifiable causes of premature cancer mortality and suffering for adults with serious mental illness.

title: Mechanistic study and therapeutic application of AIBP in AMD
text:
It has the potential to develop the first therapy to combat anti-VEGF resistance of CNV by inhibiting arteriolar
CNV, and significantly improve current anti-VEGF therapies for a broad spectrum of patients. Because anti-
VEGF therapy is the mainstay treatment for ocular vascular diseases including CNV, diabetic retinopathy, and
retinal vein occlusion, this project will have broad impact on the field of ocular angiogenic diseases.

title: Mechanisms of myocardial regeneration mediated by Nkx2.5 in zebrafish
text:
Myocardial infarction is the most prevalent sequela of ischemic heart disease and is the leading cause of
mortality in the world. Although progress has been made in understanding the endogenous regenerative
potential of cardiomyocytes, the function of extracellular milieu in cardiac repair has yet to be unraveled.
We will dissect the Nkx2.5 transcriptional pathway to uncover novel matrix proteins in zebrafish and will
exploit innate pro-regenerative mechanisms to augment cell-based transplantation therapies for patients
suffering from coronary artery disease.

title: Binding of Epstein Barr Virus EBNA2 Unifies Multiple Sclerosis Genetic Mechanisms
text:
The proposed research is relevant to human health because it will discover specific molecular events that
contribute to multiple sclerosis, leading to better diagnostics, treatments, and eventually cures. This project is
relevant to the NIH’s mission, and the mission of NINDS in particular, because it will provide fundamental insights
into the role of the Epstein-Barr virus and human genetics in the etiology of multiple sclerosis.

title: Use of the Noncanonical Amino Acid Mutagenesis Technique in Combination with Other Approaches to Study Functions of Posttranslational Lysine Modifications in Proteins
text:
The major goal of the current application is to understand functions of posttranslational lysine modifications
in the regulation of chromatin, polyubiquitination functions, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase. The project is
relevant to public health and the NIH’s mission in promoting health and combating diseases because it will reveal
the molecular basis of chromatin and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase regulation by posttranslational lysine
modifications and assist in the identification of therapeutics that target chromatin and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase
modifications.

title: Generation and validation of peptide:MHCI restricted CAR Tregs
text:
In autoimmune diabetes there is a breakdown in immunological tolerance and regulatory T cells
(Tregs) stop protecting beta cells, leaving them susceptible to immune mediated destruction. We
developed an approach to make antigen-specific Tregs by engineering mAbs into chimeric antigen
receptors targeting peptide:MHCI complexes. We successfully engineered MHCI CAR Tregs, and the
goal of this application is to validate and demonstrate the suppressive impact these Tregs can have
on CD8+ and CD4+ T cell responses to limit autoimmunity.

title: Predictive models for incident cirrhosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease using genetic and electronic medical record-based risk factors
text:
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) affects >30% of the US population and is projected to become the
leading cause of liver-related death in the US within the next 20 years; however, predicting which patients with
NAFLD ultimately develop advanced liver disease is challenging and this knowledge gap impairs allocation of
resources to the highest-risk patients. Genetics and electronic medical record-derived data may provide
additional information that assists with risk stratification, and the research proposed here will incorporate
genetics with the electronic medical record to generate predictive models for incident cirrhosis among patients
with NAFLD. Ultimately, this project will allow medical providers to better identify which patients with NAFLD
are at highest risk of progression and accordingly prioritize them for intensive therapy.

title: Mental Stress Reactivity in Women with Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction
text:
This grant proposal aims to investigate sympathetic activation with mental stress in women with
chest pain who have coronary microvascular dysfunction. Cardiac sympathetic imaging,
autonomic and vascular reactivity assessment, as well as home monitoring for autonomic
function and daily life stress are proposed. The application incorporates a multi-disciplinary
team of experts and innovative methods to study a clinical problem that disproportionately
impacts women.

title: Data Analysis & Submission Core
text: Data Analysis and Submission Core The Data Analysis and Submission Core (DASC) will assemble and validate virome characterization data for the proposed Penn VCC and submit data to public repositories and the HVP Consortium Organization and Data Collaboration Center (CODCC). The Core will be led by Drs. Kyle Bittinger and Hongzhe Li, who have a well- established track record of collaboration spanning twelve years of published work, as well as extensive collaborations with other members of the Penn VCC. Data processing will be carried out within the Analytical Laboratory of the CHOP Microbiome Center, directed by Dr. Bittinger. The Analytical Laboratory has provided bioinformatics support to hundreds of projects since its establishment in 2015. Statistical analysis and multi- omics data integration will be led by Dr. Li, who has contributed extensive innovative new methods in this space. They will process sequence data in a timely fashion from diverse samples including nucleic acid sequencing from isolated virome preparations, metagenome and 16S sample types. They will assemble and annotate sequences, and carry out first pass statistical analysis. They will apply statistical and bioinformatic approaches to interrogate longitudinal stability or evolution of the virome over multiple-year periods in children and adults; to assess the relationship between oral, respiratory tract, gut and blood compartments; and apply and refine analytical techniques to distinguish authentic from environmental background in low microbial content specimens. The team will also carry out analysis of long read single molecule sequencing to improve contig assembly and assess phage covalent DNA modification; analyze HiC data to assign viruses to hosts; and process imaging data to yield viral counts and other forms of information. The team will assess the quality of virome purifications using ViromeQC. The team will work with the other VCCs and the CODCC to establish and validate common protocols for bioinformatics and data analysis, and transfer data to the CODCC in a timely fashion. To accomplish these goals, the Aims of the Penn VCC DASC are as follows: Aim 1. Carry out bioinformatics data processing and statistical analysis to characterize the human virome and validate results. Aim 2. Construct a virome database to integrate data from a multifaceted set of experimental and computational approaches. Aim 3. Coordinate with the CODCC to develop common data formats, harmonize tools and workflows, and submit data to public repositories.

title: Technology-based assessments and intervention to reduce alcohol consumption and improve HIV viral suppression in the Florida Cohort
text:
:
The majority of persons with HIV (PWH) in the US consume alcohol, despite that alcohol use is associated with lower levels of HIV care engagement and HIV viral suppression. The overarching goals of the current grant proposal are to advance understanding of the mechanisms influencing adherence to contemporary HIV therapeutic regimens, and to incorporate alcohol-related interventions into emerging clinic- and community-based strategies to achieve and maintain HIV viral suppression across populations with varied backgrounds and needs. The rich information we collect in this project will establish a solid foundation for our next step: a hybrid implementation/effectiveness trial of an integrated alcohol intervention across a large network of clinic-/community-based HIV settings in Florida.

title: Enhancing intestinal regeneration with Cysteine mediated dietary intervention
text:
Unraveling the intricacies of nutritional status and metabolic control in tissue physiology and disease is
of utmost significance due to the global surge in metabolic dysfunction and cancer. The abundance of nutrients
plays a pivotal role in shaping both the function and physiology of tissues. This proposal has a pivotal
objective: to unravel the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the influence of dietary amino acid,
cysteine, on the intricate dynamics of intestine homeostasis and the process of tissue regeneration.

title: Human Immune Monitoring Center
text: The TCI Human Immune Monitoring Center Shared Resource (HIMCSR) is a collaborative consortium of technologists, immunologists, clinicians, and computational biologists with the coordinated goal of generating unprecedented immune profiling datasets to interrogate the etiology of cancer, novel biomarkers of disease course, and response to immunotherapy trials in cancer patients. The HIMCSR includes a range of cutting-edge high-throughput technology platforms to define circulating immune factors in blood and body fluids; characterize immune cells in blood, bone marrow and tissue samples; interrogate specific cellular, molecular immune pathways that may be dysregulated in disease; and characterize changes upon therapy or treatment. These complementary technology platforms are fully integrated with automated laboratory, biospecimen, and data management systems to facilitate detailed immune characterization of patient samples at exceptional scale with uncompromising data quality and scientific rigor. These data may be linked with cutting-edge computational, bioinformatics, and machine learning pipelines to extract meaningful and actionable therapeutic insights. The HIMCSR contributes to the TCI’s mission by providing state-of-the-art technologies, project development, consistency, interpretations, and cost-effectiveness to all TCI programs. The Specific Aims of this Shared Resource are to: (1) Provide full-service implementation of high-dimensional, state-of-the-art technologies to assess immune cell phenotypes, functionality, and changes upon treatment using cancer patient biospecimens; (2) Continuously optimize methods, instruments, reagents, analytical methods, and standard operating procedures to remain at the cutting-edge of immune monitoring approaches.

title: Designing cell-instructive viscoelastic hydrogels to understand and exploit mechanobiology
text:
Tissue mechanics directly regulate numerous cell behaviors involved in development, wound healing, and
disease progression. This proposal will develop biomaterials that mimic the dynamic properties of natural
tissues to improve our understanding of how cells sense and integrate mechanical signals from their
environment. This work should have broad implications for the development of biomaterial therapies to treat
disease and promote tissue regeneration.

title: Joint Carnegie Mellon-University of Pittsburgh Training Program in Computational Biology
text: Biomedical research has become a data-intensive field that depends on researchers with sophisticated knowledge of both computational and biomedical sciences and their intersection. By training a core of exceptionally talented students in these skills, the Joint Carnegie Mellon – University of Pittsburgh Ph.D. Program in Computational Biology has contributed to training the next generation of leaders in computational biology to help advance medical treatments that now critically depend on computational innovation, such as medical image analysis, personalized and genomic medicine, and modern drug design. Building on a track record of success, the proposed training plan would improve training by enabling the development of a new curriculum structure, develop a new scientific ethics course that addresses emerging issues in computational biology and artificial intelligence, offer further opportunities for professional development, improve recruitment and retention of training grant eligible students, and further engage students in program governance and the creation of their own customized training plans.

title: Training Program in Cardiovascular Research
text:
This program will address critical issues in cardiovascular medicine: the dwindling supply of well-trained clinical
and basic researchers focused on cardiovascular disease, and the need for investigators who can thrive in the
multi-disciplinary environments essential to current research approaches. Trainees must be facile with new
statistical approaches to large datasets and familiar with modern Omics techniques. Our ultimate goal is to
produce investigators who can not only compete successfully for extramural funding and faculty positions but
who can make substantive contributions to the understanding and treatment of cardiovascular disease, which
remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States.

title: Mechanistic association of epigenetic bone age and frailty measures with bone imaging studies using novel artificial intelligence approaches
text:
Osteoporosis, osteopenia, and fragility fractures affect more than 60 million Americans and will affect more
people as the population ages. This research will apply artificial intelligence technologies to analyze medical
imaging to identify evidence of osteoporosis earlier, when it can more easily be treated. The studies also will
determine changes in DNA called methylation that affect bone aging and the development of osteoporosis,
facilitating earlier and better diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis.

title: Elucidating mechanisms of spermatogonial stem cell competition
text:
Germline stem cells (GSCs) produce gametes that transmit alleles to the next generation, and competitive GSCs
can break Mendel’s law of equal segregation. The testis of the fruit fly Drosophila is an ideal model to study GSC
competition. Our study is designed to identify the molecular mechanisms that regulate GSC competition and
biased inheritance and may open up new therapies for treating human paternal age effect disorders caused by
competitive GSCs in older fathers.
